title: Web analytics vs product analytics
description: How marketing-site analytics differs from in-app product analytics — questions, data model, script weight, and which AnalyticsVS tools fit each job.
quickAnswer: **Web analytics** answers how people find and browse your site (pages, referrers, campaigns). **Product analytics** answers what signed-in users do inside the product (activation, funnels, retention). Plausible and Fathom are web-first; PostHog is product-first; GA4 can span both with more setup.

sections.title: Two jobs, two dashboards
sections.content:
If your team asks "which blog posts drive signup clicks?" you need **web analytics**.

If your team asks "what percent of new workspaces invite a teammate in seven days?" you need **product analytics**.

Using one tool for both is possible (GA4, PostHog) but not free — instrumentation, privacy review, and script weight all go up. Many teams run a light web tool on the marketing site and a product tool in the app.

sections.title: Data model differences
sections.content:
Web tools optimize for **URLs, referrers, UTM campaigns, and goals**.

Product tools optimize for **named events, user/account identity, funnels, retention, and often session replay or flags**.

See [Pageviews vs Events: Which Should You Track?](/learn/pageviews-vs-events/) for the vocabulary bridge.

sections.title: Cost and script weight
sections.content:
Lightweight web tags (Plausible, Fathom, DataFast) sit in our light [script performance](/learn/analytics-script-performance/) cluster. PostHog’s default web SDK is much heavier because it ships product capabilities — fine in an app shell, often excessive on a brochure homepage.

Price units differ too: pageview tiers vs event volume. Check the [pricing calculator](/calculators/pricing/).

sections.title: How to pick a lane
sections.content:
1. List the three decisions you make weekly from analytics.
2. If they are traffic/campaign decisions → start web-first ([Plausible vs PostHog](/compare/posthog-vs-plausible/) explains the mismatch).
3. If they are activation/retention decisions → start product-first ([GA4 vs PostHog](/compare/google-analytics-vs-posthog/)).
4. Add a second tool only when the first lane is clearly insufficient.
